details: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for May 2026 rose 4.2% year-over-year, marking the highest inflation rate in three years. This increase, largely driven by energy costs, met economists' forecasts. The persistent elevated inflation reinforces expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain its current hawkish monetary policy and keep interest rates steady, limiting upside potential and increasing volatility for risk assets like cryptocurrencies. Core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy, rose 0.2% month-over-month, slightly below forecasts, suggesting underlying price pressures might be easing at the margins.
title: US May CPI Surges to 4.2%, Reinforcing Hawkish Fed Stance

details: Tether's (USDT) market dominance spiked by 13.5% last week to 9%, its largest weekly increase since March 2025. This surge coincided with a sharp Bitcoin sell-off that briefly pushed BTC below $60,000. Crucially, Tether's overall market capitalization declined for a third consecutive week, indicating that investors are converting crypto holdings into fiat currencies and exiting the market entirely, rather than simply rotating into stablecoins as a temporary hedge against volatility.
title: Tether Dominance Surges as Capital Exits Crypto Market

details: While tech and AI-linked equities experienced a significant rebound, with the Nasdaq 100 climbing 1.6% and semiconductor indices gaining over 5%, the cryptocurrency market largely failed to participate in this renewed risk appetite. Bitcoin saw only a modest 0.8% increase, trading near $63,300, while Ethereum rose 1.8%. This decoupling suggests that capital is flowing back into traditional growth assets rather than digital assets, signaling diminished investor confidence in crypto's immediate prospects.
title: Crypto Lags Tech Rebound Despite AI Stock Bounce

details: Polish President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed a cryptocurrency regulation bill for the third time, delaying the implementation of the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) framework in Poland. The President expressed support for regulation but cited unmet amendment suggestions, creating ongoing uncertainty for the country's crypto sector. Conversely, Hungary is preparing to roll back restrictive measures on its cryptocurrency market, with plans to remove criminal penalties for unauthorized crypto services. This policy shift aims to reduce compliance costs and align with the EU's MiCA framework, potentially improving regulatory predictability in Central Europe.
title: Poland's President Vetoes Crypto Bill, Hungary Reverses Restrictions

details: In the past 24 hours, cryptocurrency futures contracts saw $438 million in liquidations, with the majority impacting long positions. Bitcoin futures accounted for $14.6 million in liquidations, Ethereum for $10.2 million, Solana for $13.36 million, and XRP for $10.31 million. Such significant liquidations typically occur during periods of high volatility and indicate forced selling, putting downward pressure on prices and signaling caution in the derivatives market.
title: $438 Million in Crypto Futures Liquidated in 24 Hours

details: Bitcoin's Market Value to Realized Value (MVRV) ratio is currently at 1.149, indicating that the average holder is up by approximately 14.9%. This level is close to Bitcoin's cost basis, a zone that has historically coincided with market bottoms and accumulation periods. The one-year MVRV view shows holders are down 34%, a level classified as a "generational bottom," suggesting potential for long-term value buying if historical patterns hold.
title: Bitcoin's MVRV Ratio Nears Historical Accumulation Zone
